data.body_html:
Choosing between the Azimut 39 and the Fairline Targa 12m for your Marbella boat charter? Both depart from Puerto Banús and offer superb days on the Costa del Sol, but they suit different styles. This 2046 comparison breaks down the key differences – from passenger capacity to pricing – so you can book with confidence.

Azimut 39 vs Fairline Targa 12m: Key specs at a glance

Here’s the quick comparison. Both are premium motor yachts, but the Azimut 39 is a flybridge cruiser, while the Fairline Targa 12m is an open-top sports cruiser.

FeatureAzimut 39Fairline Targa 12m
Length12.5m12m
Passengers1110
Departure pointPuerto BanúsPuerto Banús
StyleFlybridge cruiserOpen sports cruiser
Price (2h)€749On request
Price (8h)€2,299On request

Passenger capacity and space

The Azimut 39 comfortably seats 11 passengers, making it ideal for slightly larger groups – think family gatherings or a day with friends. Its flybridge offers an upper deck with additional seating and panoramic views, plus a shaded cockpit below. The Fairline Targa 12m, with 10 passengers, has a sleek, low-profile design that feels more intimate. The open cockpit is great for sunbathing, but there’s less covered space, so you’ll want sunscreen and hats.

Onboard comfort and amenities

Both boats come with the same all-inclusive package: licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and 21% IVA. The Azimut 39’s flybridge provides a shaded lounge area – perfect for escaping the midday sun. The Fairline Targa 12m, being an open design, puts you closer to the sea, with wind-in-your-hair cruising. It has a small cabin below for changing or a quick rest, but the focus is on the outdoor experience.

Performance and handling

While we don’t publish official speed figures, the Fairline Targa 12m is known for its sporty, agile handling – a great choice if you want a more dynamic ride along the coast. The Azimut 39, with its flybridge and longer hull, prioritises stability and smooth cruising. Both are perfectly capable of reaching Cabopino, Estepona, or even Sotogrande for a longer day out.

Which boat suits which group?

  • Choose the Azimut 39 if you have up to 11 guests, want shaded areas, and prefer a relaxed, stable cruise with flybridge views.
  • Choose the Fairline Targa 12m if your group is up to 10 and you value an open-air, sporty feel – ideal for younger groups or those who love the sensation of speed.

Pricing and value

The Azimut 39 offers transparent, fixed pricing: €749 for 2 hours and €2,299 for 8 hours. That’s excellent value given the inclusions. The Fairline Targa 12m is priced on request – contact us via WhatsApp for a tailored quote. Both boats are from our [Marbella fleet](/), and you can compare them with other options like the Astondoa 40 or the Azimut 58 Flybridge.

Booking and flexibility

All charters depart from Puerto Banús, the heart of Marbella’s luxury marina. You can book either boat for a half-day (2-4 hours) or a full day (8 hours). Your skipper will tailor the itinerary – whether you want to anchor at Cala del Faro for a swim, cruise past the Golden Mile, or head to Cabopino for lunch. For the Fairline Targa 12m, simply message us on WhatsApp to get a quote and check availability.

Frequently asked questions

What is the main difference between the Azimut 39 and Fairline Targa 12m?

The Azimut 39 is a flybridge-style cruiser with a longer hull (12.5m) and seats 11 passengers, while the Fairline Targa 12m is a sporty open-cockpit boat (12m) that seats 10. The Azimut offers more shaded deck space, making it better for larger groups, while the Fairline is more agile and sporty.

How much does it cost to charter the Azimut 39 in Marbella?

The Azimut 39 is priced at €749 for 2 hours and €2,299 for 8 hours. This includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and Spanish IVA. No hidden costs.

How much does it cost to charter the Fairline Targa 12m?

Pricing for the Fairline Targa 12m is on request – contact us via WhatsApp for a tailored quote. The price includes the same all-inclusive package: skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and VAT.

Which boat is better for a large group – Azimut 39 or Fairline Targa 12m?

If you have 11 passengers, the Azimut 39 is the better choice as it accommodates one more person and offers more covered seating. The Fairline Targa 12m is ideal for groups of up to 10 who prefer an open, sportier deck experience.

Can I take either boat to Cabopino or Estepona?

Yes, both boats can cruise along the coast to Cabopino, Estepona, or even Sotogrande. The Azimut 39's flybridge provides great views, while the Fairline Targa 12m offers a more immersive, open-air ride. Your skipper will plan the route based on weather and your preferences.

Are there any hidden fees for these charters?

No. The listed prices (or quoted prices for the Fairline) are all-inclusive. You pay only the charter fee – no extra for fuel, skipper, drinks, snacks, or insurance. The only optional extras are things like jet skis, which are available on some boats.

Which boat is faster: Azimut 39 or Fairline Targa 12m?

The Fairline Targa 12m is typically sportier and can reach higher speeds, making it a fun choice for thrill-seekers. The Azimut 39 is more of a comfortable cruiser, focusing on stability and relaxation rather than top-end speed.
